To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

distributed embedded systems for low energy consumption must consider the tradeoff between energy savings and battery lifetime, and that the key to achieving a longer battery life is to balance the discharge rate among the nodes.
distributed embedded systems can create new Dvs opportunities and achieve further power savings, but the energy savings do not necessarily translate into a longer battery lifetime.

(1) a distributed embedded system can achieve further energy savings with dynamic voltage scaling; (2) a distributed system can achieve further battery lifetime improvements by distributing the workload onto multiple nodes and balancing the discharge rates of the nodes; (3) a distributed system cannot always achieve a higher energy efficiency than a single-processor system; and (4) the aggregate energy savings do NOT translate into a longer battery lifetime
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of distributed embedded systems for low energy.
how to design and evaluate a distributed embedded system that can achieve low power.
the design, analysis, and evaluation of distributed embedded systems for low-power operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the benefits of DVS on a distributed system is highly dependent on the application.
a distributed system is not always the most effective way to achieve energy savings.
the distributed nature of a system can create new opportunities for DVS, but it is not a panacea for achieving higher energy savings or longer battery life
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DVS can be effective for distributed systems, but the energy savings must be carefully translated to battery life improvements.
the distributed embedded system can create new opportunities for DVS.
the benefits of DVS in distributed embedded systems are limited by the cost of communications and the need for a balanced battery discharge rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multiple-processor system is not a panacea for energy savings, and a distributed system must be designed with the battery life in mind.
energy savings in distributed systems are not as straightforward to realize as in single processors.
the design of the communication system has a significant impact on the energy efficiency of distributed embedded systems.
